item.title: 'Shave ICE' for a cause: Asato’s raising money for immigrant support groups
item.description: Asato’s Waikiki, a popular shave ice shop, announced it will donate 100% of its profits to local organizations that support immigrants and families negatively impacted by recent ICE activity and rising fears within the community.

item.title: HFD responds to late night car fire at Keaau Beach Park
item.description: Honolulu firefighters responded to a car fire at Keaau Beach Park late Saturday night, Jan. 31.

item.title: Police officer killed, another seriously wounded in hotel room shootout in Georgia
item.description: LAWRENCEVILLE, Ga. item.title: North Shore community to support surfer Dakota Briley at fundraiser festival
item.description: The North Shore community is continuing to rally around one of its own as 20-year-old Dakota Briley continues through a long and challenging recovery following a devastating accident last summer.

item.title: Beware of phishing scam posing as Hawaiʻi DMV over “unpaid traffic fines”
item.description: The County of Kauaʻi's Finance Department wants to warn residents of a phishing text scam falsely claiming to be from the Hawaiʻi Department of Motor Vehicles.

item.title: Man, 84, seriously injured in single vehicle collision: EMS
item.description: An 84-year-old man was seriously injured in a single-vehicle collision on the Pali Highway.

item.title: New UHERO report finds Hawaiʻi's economy has "lagged behind the rest of the U.S. for years"
item.description: According to a new report from the University of Hawaiʻi's Economic Research Organization, Hawaii's economy is among the worst in the nation.

item.title: Man, 33, rescued after head injury on ʻUluwehi Falls Trail
item.description: A visitor was rescued on the ʻUluwehi Falls Trail after hitting his head in the water at the falls.

item.title: Search continues for suspects involved in burglary of popular Aiea restaurant
item.description: The search continues for three suspects wanted in a burglary at a popular Aiea restaurant. Employees say the break-in has left them shaken and concerned about safety moving forward.
